subject: Proposal: One-time credit + 9-month term reset + SLA overlay for LumenEx renewal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: approval for LumenEx renewal concessions (credit + term reset + SLA)

Team —

Quick summary: LumenEx (current ARR $1.45M, renew date 2026-10-10) is asking for a preservation package to stay with Redwood. They came back with a competing offer from a lower-cost managed provider and are asking for non-standard commercial terms. The AE/CS asks I escalate for executive approval.

Proposed concession package (account request + our recommended guardrails):
- One-time credit: $120,000 applied up front to next invoice (approx 8.3% of ARR) — requested by customer to offset migration costs.
- Term reset: convert remaining 6 months on current contract into a new 12-month renewal at current list price (effectively extends the commitment window; reduces near-term churn risk).
- SLA overlay: 99.95% availability guarantee for core API routes for 12 months with credits capped at 1.5x monthly invoice for SLA breaches.

Rationales:
- Customer has heavy usage spikes tied to product seasonality; losing them will also risk a larger multi-account procurement with a partner in their stack.
- We have technical improvements planned that will reduce their burst costs next quarter; a credit + term reset gives us time to realize ops improvements.
- Competitive pressure is real: LumenEx provided a written cheaper alternative and a timeline to decide (10/08).

Financials / mitigations:
- One-time credit is limited to $120k and contingent on immediate signature of the new 12-month agreement (no partial acceptance).
- Any SLA credit payments will be paid out of a central concession bucket and must be reported to Deal Desk monthly.
- We require a joint MOP (mutual action plan) and a technical checkpoint at 60 days; SLA addendum to be run by Legal/RevOps (attached v2).

Files attached: LumenEx_Savings_Breakdown_Q3.pdf, Proposed_SLA_Addendum_v2.docx, Mutual_Action_Plan_LumenEx.xlsx

Ask: Executive sign-off to offer the package above and authority to commit up to $125k of one-time concession. If approved, I will prepare final redline and DocuSign packet and set the 60-day ops checkpoint.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <mononica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: approval for LumenEx renewal concessions (credit + term reset + SLA)

Karthik —

Thanks for the concise packet. A few quick clarifications before I greenlight to Vivek:

1) Is the $120k credit back-loaded or applied up front? (need billing ops clarity)
2) Does the term reset include any pricing change (we should keep list pricing and avoid ad hoc discounts on unit rates)
3) Can Legal confirm the SLA credit cap language is consistent with precedent (I flagged the 1.5x monthly cap as slightly generous; prefer 1x unless customer insists)

Recommended adjustments for approval:
- Make credit conditional on execution and 30 days of continued platform usage (to deter transient sign-and-run behavior).
- Keep list pricing for the new term; provide a one-time credit rather than lowering unit rates.
- Change SLA credit cap to 1x monthly invoice; escalate to me if Legal pushes back.

If those adjustments are acceptable, I will recommend approval for up to $125k total concession authority.

Marissa
VP, Sales — Americas
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik —

I reviewed the ask and the attachment deck. We should prioritize retention here; the account is strategic and the churn risk is material. Approve with the conditions Marissa outlined, plus one addendum:

- Approval granted for a maximum $125,000 one-time concession, payable as a credit at contract signature.
- SLA credit cap adjusted to 1x monthly invoice. Legal to confirm final SLA language; RevOps to document concession in Deal Desk ledger.
- Require a 60-day technical health checkpoint and a 90-day executive QBR (I will join). If LumenEx violates the usage covenant (fails to maintain minimum usage threshold in MAP), the remaining term reverts to original cancellation terms.

Karthik — take to Legal for the SLA redline, prep DocuSign with the condition language and the MAP attached; once DocuSign packet is ready, execute and confirm with me.

Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
